source: 25 August 2026 Memorial tribute Home.tsx partner grid

categories.category: THE FORGE — Personal Tools That Built iAAi

partners.name: Shokz
partners.text: Bone conduction headsets — 10,000+ hours of audio learning while walking, running, and thinking. The ears stayed open to the world while the mind absorbed civilisations.

partners.name: HP
partners.text: Beamer glasses and displays — the visual interface where every iCard, every thesis, every equation was composed and reviewed at arm’s length.

partners.name: Garmin
partners.text: Fenix Solar — the wrist-mounted command centre. GPS, heart rate, solar charging. Every walk, every field operation, every block logged and timestamped.

partners.name: Apple
partners.text: iPhone — the capture device. Every screenshot, every WhatsApp thread, every photograph of ashes cast into the ocean. The camera that never blinked.

partners.name: Lenovo
partners.text: ThinkPad × Intel — the workhorse. The machine that ran the simulations, compiled the documents, and never crashed when it mattered most.

partners.name: Intel
partners.text: The processor inside the machine. Intel’s silicon foundation powered 40 years of computing — every simulation, every compile, every render.

partners.name: Omega
partners.text: Speedmaster — the watch that went to the moon. Timekeeping as engineering discipline. Every second measured, every mission timed.

partners.name: Seiko
partners.text: Spring Drive — the movement that bridges mechanical and electronic. Japanese precision engineering at the wrist. Craftsmanship as philosophy.

partners.name: Dyson
partners.text: Engineering without compromise. 5,127 prototypes before the first vacuum worked. That’s the iAAi method — iterate until it’s right.

partners.name: Sony
partners.text: Walkman to PlayStation. Sony invented personal audio and then personal gaming — two revolutions in consciousness delivery.

partners.name: Samsung
partners.text: Displays, chips, phones, appliances. The Korean conglomerate that builds everything from the screen you’re reading to the memory inside it.

categories.category: THE DIGITAL ARCHITECTURE — AI, Cloud & Software

partners.name: Manus AI
partners.text: The AI development infrastructure — the forge where DAVID was born, where 670+ iCards were generated, where the entire digital architecture of TRE was assembled.

partners.name: Google
partners.text: Search, Maps, Earth, Translate, Scholar. The index of human knowledge — and the engine that made 120,000 hours of research possible.

partners.name: Microsoft
partners.text: Windows, Office, Teams, Azure. The operating system of modern work — 40 years of infrastructure that every engineer depends on.

partners.name: Meta
partners.text: The metaverse thesis. Whether you agree or not, Meta forced the conversation about digital presence, VR, and the next interface layer.

partners.name: Adobe
partners.text: Creative Suite — Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign. Every visual asset, every layout, every design language refined through Adobe’s tools.

partners.name: Amazon
partners.text: From bookshop to everything store to AWS. Amazon built the cloud infrastructure that runs half the internet — including this.

partners.name: Autodesk
partners.text: BIM 360 — Building Information Modelling. The digital twin of physical infrastructure. Every beam, every pipe, every connection modelled before it’s built.

partners.name: Cisco
partners.text: The plumbing of the internet. Every router, every switch, every packet. Cisco built the network layer that connects 5 billion people.

partners.name: Starlink
partners.text: SpaceX satellite internet — connectivity from orbit. Starlink proved that infrastructure can be deployed from space to serve the unserved.

partners.name: Disney
partners.text: The multi-sensory experience blueprint. Theme parks as consciousness architecture — Disney proved that immersion teaches more than instruction.

partners.name: Marvel
partners.text: The cinematic universe model. Interconnected narratives, character arcs across decades, and the proof that a shared universe scales.

partners.name: DreamWorks
partners.text: Animation as engineering. DreamWorks showed that imagination rendered at scale becomes infrastructure for the mind.

partners.name: MGM
partners.text: Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer — Ars Gratia Artis. The lion that roared for a century. MGM built the golden age of cinema and proved that storytelling is infrastructure.

partners.name: HBO
partners.text: Home Box Office — It’s not TV, it’s HBO. The Sopranos, The Wire, Game of Thrones. HBO proved that long-form narrative is the highest art form.

partners.name: Netflix
partners.text: From DVD mailer to streaming empire. Netflix rewired how 230 million people consume stories — and proved that distribution is as important as creation.

partners.name: BBC
partners.text: The world’s public broadcaster — 100 years of trusted information infrastructure. From radio to digital, the BBC set the standard.

partners.name: ESPN
partners.text: Sports broadcasting infrastructure — live events at global scale. ESPN made sport a 24-hour information system.

categories.category: THE RECORD KEEPERS — News, Publishing & Media

partners.name: Reuters
partners.text: The wire service — raw information at the speed of light since 1851. Reuters built the nervous system of global news.

partners.name: AP
partners.text: The Associated Press — the cooperative that feeds every newsroom on Earth. 175 years of factual infrastructure.

partners.name: Bloomberg
partners.text: Financial data infrastructure — the terminal that runs Wall Street. Bloomberg turned information into the most valuable commodity.

partners.name: Al Jazeera
partners.text: The Eastern lens — news infrastructure from Doha to the world. Al Jazeera proved that perspective is infrastructure.

partners.name: The Times
partners.text: The newspaper of record since 1785 — London’s voice for 240 years. The Times defined what ‘news’ means.

partners.name: Wall Street Journal
partners.text: The Wall Street Journal — the financial paper of record. Markets as infrastructure, reported daily since 1889.

partners.name: Washington Post
partners.text: Democracy dies in darkness — the Washington Post. Political infrastructure reporting that holds power accountable.

partners.name: TIME
partners.text: TIME Magazine — the Person of the Year. 100 years of framing who matters and why.

partners.name: National Geographic
partners.text: 135 years of exploration documented. National Geographic proved that storytelling and science are the same discipline when done at the highest level.

partners.name: Nature
partners.text: Nature — the world’s most cited scientific journal since 1869. Where breakthroughs are published, peer-reviewed, and made permanent.

partners.name: Science
partners.text: Science (AAAS) — the journal that published Watson & Crick, the Human Genome, and the first image of a black hole.

partners.name: The Lancet
partners.text: The Lancet — medical science’s journal of record since 1823. 200 years of evidence-based infrastructure for human health.

partners.name: IEEE
partners.text: IEEE — the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. 400,000 members, the standards body that defines how technology communicates.

partners.name: ASCE
partners.text: ASCE — the American Society of Civil Engineers. Founded 1852. The professional home of infrastructure engineering worldwide.

categories.category: THE MUSEUMS — Permanent Archives of Human Achievement

partners.name: Smithsonian
partners.text: The world’s largest museum complex — 154 million artefacts. The Smithsonian is the permanent archive of human achievement. The Vault’s spiritual ancestor.

partners.name: British Museum
partners.text: The British Museum — 8 million objects, the Rosetta Stone, the Parthenon Marbles. The world’s first public national museum, est. 1753.

partners.name: The Louvre
partners.text: The Louvre — the most visited museum on Earth. 380,000 objects, 35,000 on display. The Mona Lisa lives here, but so does civilisation’s memory.

partners.name: The Met
partners.text: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — 2 million works spanning 5,000 years. New York’s cultural infrastructure, open to the world.

partners.name: Hermitage
partners.text: The State Hermitage Museum — 3 million items across 6 buildings on the Neva. Russia’s cultural fortress, founded by Catherine the Great.

partners.name: Guggenheim
partners.text: The Guggenheim — Frank Lloyd Wright’s spiral in New York, Gehry’s titanium in Bilbao. Architecture as art, art as infrastructure.

partners.name: M+ Museum HK
partners.text: M+ Museum Hong Kong — Asia’s largest museum of visual culture. 65,000 sq m of consciousness architecture on the Victoria Harbour waterfront.

partners.name: British Library
partners.text: 170 million items. The British National Library holds the Magna Carta, the Gutenberg Bible, and Leonardo’s notebooks. Knowledge preserved is civilisation preserved.

partners.name: Library of Congress
partners.text: The Library of Congress — 170 million items, the largest library on Earth. America’s memory, and the world’s reference.

partners.name: BnF (France)
partners.text: Bibliothèque nationale de France — 40 million documents. The French national library, guardian of European intellectual heritage since 1461.

partners.name: NDL (Japan)
partners.text: National Diet Library of Japan — the legal deposit library of Japan. Eastern knowledge preserved with Japanese precision.

partners.name: NLC (China)
partners.text: National Library of China — 37 million items. 5,000 years of continuous civilisation, archived and indexed.

partners.name: Royal Society
partners.text: The Royal Society — est. 1660. Newton, Darwin, Hawking. The oldest scientific institution in continuous existence. Nullius in verba — take nobody’s word for it.

partners.name: NASA
partners.text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration — from Mercury to Mars. NASA proved that infrastructure extends beyond the atmosphere.

partners.name: CERN
partners.text: The European Organization for Nuclear Research — the Large Hadron Collider. CERN built the machine that found the Higgs boson and invented the World Wide Web.

partners.name: SETI
partners.text: The Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence — listening to the cosmos. SETI is infrastructure for the question that defines us: are we alone?

partners.name: Red Cross
partners.text: The International Red Cross — humanitarian infrastructure since 1863. 192 national societies, 14 million volunteers. When civilisation breaks, the Red Cross holds.

partners.name: United Nations
partners.text: The United Nations — the global governance framework. 193 member states, one planetary infrastructure.

partners.name: UN SDGs
partners.text: 17 Sustainable Development Goals — the planetary checklist. ISI₁ maps directly to the UN SDG framework. The survival index starts here.

partners.name: WHO
partners.text: World Health Organization — health infrastructure for 8 billion people. WHO coordinates the survival of the species.

partners.name: WWF
partners.text: World Wildlife Fund — conservation infrastructure, planetary stewardship. The panda that guards the biosphere.

partners.name: World Bank
partners.text: The World Bank — development infrastructure for 189 member countries. $70 billion annually to build the foundations of emerging economies.

partners.name: Nobel Prize
partners.text: The Nobel Prize — the highest recognition of human achievement since 1901. The gold standard of intellectual infrastructure.

partners.name: Olympics
partners.text: The Olympic Games — the oldest continuous human competition. 3,000 years of athletic infrastructure, from Olympia to Paris.

partners.name: FIFA
partners.text: 5 billion viewers — the most-watched event in human history. FIFA proved that sport is the universal language of infrastructure.

partners.name: JPMorgan Chase
partners.text: JPMorgan Chase — 225 years of financial infrastructure. The bank that survived every crisis and still moves $6 trillion daily.

partners.name: HSBC
partners.text: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation — East meets West since 1865. The financial bridge between civilisations.

partners.name: Wells Fargo
partners.text: Stagecoach to digital banking. Wells Fargo moved gold across the frontier and now moves capital across the planet — 163 years of financial infrastructure.

partners.name: Rolls-Royce
partners.text: Engineering excellence — aero engines that power half the world’s wide-body aircraft. The Spirit of Ecstasy is a thesis in metal.

partners.name: Aston Martin
partners.text: British engineering art — the DB5 is a thesis in aluminium. Aston Martin proved that beauty and engineering are the same discipline.

partners.name: Lotus
partners.text: Colin Chapman’s philosophy — simplify, then add lightness. Lotus proved that less is more when the engineering is right.

partners.name: Bentley
partners.text: Continental GT — luxury as engineering, not decoration. Bentley builds machines that cross continents in silence.

partners.name: Maserati
partners.text: The trident — Italian engineering passion. Neptune’s weapon forged in Modena. Maserati is sound as infrastructure.

partners.name: Porsche
partners.text: 911 — 60 years of the same silhouette, perfected every generation. Porsche proved that evolution beats revolution.

partners.name: BMW
partners.text: The Ultimate Driving Machine — Bayerische Motoren Werke. BMW engineered the connection between human and road.

partners.name: Mercedes-Benz
partners.text: The first automobile — Benz Patent-Motorwagen 1886. Mercedes-Benz invented the category and still defines it.

partners.name: Tesla
partners.text: Electric revolution — Musk proved the incumbents wrong. Tesla made sustainable transport desirable, not dutiful.

partners.name: GE
partners.text: Edison’s company — power generation, aviation, healthcare. GE built the infrastructure that electrified the world.

categories.category: THE LIFESTYLE ARCHITECTS — Luxury, Travel & Commerce

partners.name: Tiffany & Co.
partners.text: The standard of craft. When you name something Tiffany-class, everyone knows what you mean — precision, permanence, and zero compromise.

partners.name: Virgin
partners.text: Branson’s empire — music, airlines, space. The proof that one brand can span every domain if the founder’s vision is strong enough.

partners.name: Alibaba
partners.text: The Eastern bridge. Alibaba connected 10 million SMEs to global trade — infrastructure at civilisational scale, built from Hangzhou.

partners.name: WeWork
partners.text: The shared workspace where ideas collided with strangers. Co-working as consciousness accelerator — proximity breeds innovation.
